before_EC.when: Arizona exemptions are allowable and the asset is a firearm, motor vehicle, apparel item, or item of jewelry.
before_EC.procedure: Classify by the statutory category: firearms under Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10), each motor vehicle as a candidate under § 33-1125(8), wearing apparel under § 33-1125(1), and only engagement or wedding rings under § 33-1125(4). In EC, a value or aggregate ceiling limits protection rather than citation eligibility, and the one-vehicle language does not require final portfolio allocation among separately listed vehicle candidates.
before_EC.avoid_when: Do not reject an otherwise matching firearm or vehicle solely for exceeding its ceiling. Do not treat a pendant, bracelet, or other non-apparel adornment as wearing apparel, and do not extend the ring exemption to jewelry that is not an engagement or wedding ring.

proposed_EC.when: Arizona exemptions are allowable and the asset is a firearm, motor vehicle, apparel item, or item of jewelry.
proposed_EC.procedure: Classify physical character before considering value: use Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10) for firearms, (8) for each motor-vehicle candidate, (1) only for actual garments or footwear, and (4) only when facts expressly identify an engagement or wedding ring. Pendants, necklaces, bracelets, earrings, lockets, brooches, and other adornments get neither (1), (4), nor household-goods § 33-1123 merely because they are worn or personal. A ceiling limits protection, not EC citation eligibility.
proposed_EC.avoid_when: Do not reject an otherwise matching firearm or vehicle solely for exceeding its ceiling. Do not treat a pendant, bracelet, or other non-apparel adornment as wearing apparel, and do not extend the ring exemption to jewelry that is not an engagement or wedding ring.

before_EC.when: Federal exemptions are an allowable namespace and the facts show a debtor interest in an estate asset.
before_EC.procedure: After classifying specific exemptions, make a separate asset-by-asset wildcard pass. Add 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) for every debtor-owned asset because it covers any property, including residences, vehicles, household goods, jewelry, firearms, tools and health aids; retain every independently applicable specific federal or state citation. Its ceiling limits protected value, not EC eligibility.
before_EC.avoid_when: Skip § 522(d)(5) only when federal exemptions are unavailable or the facts do not show a debtor interest. Do not skip it because another exemption applies or the asset exceeds the ceiling.

proposed_EC.when: Federal exemptions are an allowable namespace and the facts show a debtor interest in an estate asset.
proposed_EC.procedure: Initialize every debtor-owned asset's EC array with 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) before testing specific exemptions. Then add every matching specific federal or state citation; never remove (d)(5) because another citation applies or because the asset exceeds its ceiling. The ceiling limits protected value, not EC eligibility.
proposed_EC.avoid_when: Skip § 522(d)(5) only when federal exemptions are unavailable or the facts do not show a debtor interest. Do not skip it because another exemption applies or the asset exceeds the ceiling.

before_EC.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
before_EC.procedure: After classifying specific exemptions, make a separate § 12-1001(b) pass over every qualifying personal-property asset. Add 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) alongside any motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel or prescribed-health-aid citation, as well as for jewelry and other personal property. Its $4,000 ceiling limits protected equity, not EC eligibility.
before_EC.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real property or property the facts explicitly identify as business-use. Do not omit it because a specific exemption applies, and do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel.

proposed_EC.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
proposed_EC.procedure: First add 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) to every qualifying asset, before classifying its type or value. Retain it while adding any matching motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel, or prescribed-health-aid citation. Its $4,000 ceiling limits protected equity, not EC eligibility.
proposed_EC.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real property or property the facts explicitly identify as business-use. Do not omit it because a specific exemption applies, and do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel. A personal appliance is not a trade tool without business-use facts.

before_EC.when: Oregon exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property.
before_EC.procedure: After checking category-specific Oregon exemptions, make a separate pass over every personal-property asset and add Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p). Retain it alongside clothing, household-goods, vehicle, animal, firearm, jewelry, instrument, health-aid and other specific alternatives. Its $400 ceiling limits protected value, not EC eligibility.
before_EC.avoid_when: Do not apply § 18.345(1)(p) to real property. Do not omit it because another Oregon exemption applies or because the personal property's value exceeds $400.

proposed_EC.when: Oregon exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property.
proposed_EC.procedure: Initialize every such asset's EC array with Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) before classifying its category or considering value. Then add every matching category-specific Oregon citation; never remove (1)(p) because another exemption applies or the asset exceeds $400.
proposed_EC.avoid_when: Do not apply § 18.345(1)(p) to real property. Do not omit it because another Oregon exemption applies or because the personal property's value exceeds $400.

before_EC.when: Pennsylvania exemptions are allowable and the facts show a debtor interest in an estate asset.
before_EC.procedure: After checking particular-property exemptions, make a separate § 8123 pass over every debtor-owned asset, including real property, vehicles, household goods, jewelry and business tools. Add 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 alongside every applicable specific citation; its $300 ceiling limits protected value, not EC eligibility.
before_EC.avoid_when: Skip § 8123 only when Pennsylvania exemptions are unavailable or the property is not the debtor's. Do not omit it because a specific exemption applies or the asset is worth more than $300.

proposed_EC.when: Pennsylvania exemptions are allowable and the facts show a debtor interest in an estate asset.
proposed_EC.procedure: Initialize every debtor-owned asset's EC array with 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 before checking its type or value. Then add every applicable specific citation; never remove § 8123 because another exemption applies or the asset exceeds $300. The ceiling limits protected value, not EC eligibility.
proposed_EC.avoid_when: Skip § 8123 only when Pennsylvania exemptions are unavailable or the property is not the debtor's. Do not omit it because a specific exemption applies or the asset is worth more than $300.
